title: Cap. VI Arg. 7: from the absurdity — election suspended on human faith yields no fixed elect number
pass_a_gloss: Seventhly, we argue from the inconvenience or absurdity under which this opinion of theirs labors who suspend the act of Divine election upon the preceding act of human faith and perseverance. For from this it would follow that neither the formal nor the material number of the elect is certain and defined according to some decree of Divine good pleasure, but that these singular persons, and in this defined number, are saved, happened by accident, namely from a contingent act of human choice, God foreseeing, not preordaining.
pass_b_english: Seventh argument: from the absurdity their view labors under — hanging divine election on a prior act of human faith and perseverance. Then neither the formal nor the material number of the elect would be fixed by any decree of divine good pleasure; that these particular persons are saved, and in this fixed count, would be an accident of contingent human choice — God foreseeing, not preordaining.
source_text: Septimo, argumentamur ab inconveniente vel absurdo, quo laborat haec eorum sententia qui suspendunt actum electionis Divinae ex praeeunte actu fidei ac perseverantiae humanae. Hinc enim sequeretur, nec formalem nec materialem numerum electorum esse certum ac definitum secundum decretum aliquod beneplaciti Divini, sed quod hae singulares personae, et hoc definito numero, salventur, id per accidens evenisse, ex contingente nimirum actu arbitrii humani, Deo praevidente, non praeordinante.
